title: A fluorescence recovery after photobleaching protocol to measure surface diffusion of DAGLα in primary cultured cortical mouse neurons
protocol: Decapitate postnatal day 0 (P0) mouse pups in a biosafety cabinet using surgical scissors.
Place the head into a petri dish filled with ice-cold L-15 medium.
Remove the scalp and immerse the brain in a new petri dish containing cold L-15 medium.
Transfer cortices to a 15 mL conical tube using forceps under a stereomicroscope.
Sterilize the 15 mL conical tube with 70% ethanol.
Carefully remove the L-15 medium from the cortices and add 300–400 μL of pre-warmed 0.25% trypsin.
Incubate at 37°C for 10 min.
Re-sterilize the conical tube with 70% ethanol after incubation.
Remove trypsin from the conical tube using a pipette and fill with 1 mL of pre-warmed high-glucose complete DMEM.
Mechanically dissociate cortical tissue to individual cells using a pipette.
Resuspend cells by pipetting up and down gently with a 1 mL tip placed close to the bottom of the conical tube, performing no more than 10 repetitions.
Add 4 mL of high-glucose complete DMEM and filter it using a 40 μm nylon cell strainer into a 50 mL conical tube.
Transfer 10 μL of solution from the 50 mL conical tube to an Eppendorf tube and add 10 μl of trypan blue solution.
Count live cells using a hemocytometer and calculate the number of cells per mL in the 50 mL conical tube.
Seed 1.333 × 10^5 cells/cm² on the PDL-coated coverslip.
Fill each well of a 12-well plate with up to 1 mL of high-glucose medium.
Fill the four corner wells of the 12-well plate with autoclaved distilled water to mitigate evaporation of the medium.
Transfer the 12-well plate to the incubator at 37°C with 5% CO₂ and wait for 2 hours for neuronal precursor cells to settle on the PDL-coated coverslip.
Check the adhesion of precursors to the coverslip using an epi-illumination microscope after 2 hours.
Remove high-glucose complete DMEM carefully and replace with 1 mL of pre-warmed complete neurobasal medium.
Maintain primary cortical neuron culture in the incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 21 days.
Replace complete neurobasal medium twice a week.
Prepare solutions for transfection in advance.
Mix h-DMEM and transfection neurobasal medium separately in two different Eppendorf tubes.
Combine 2 μg total of plasmids (e.g., 1 μg SEP-DAGLα + 1 μg mCherry) with transfection neurobasal medium.
Mix 2 μL lipofectamine 2000 per sample in h-DMEM.
Mix the h-DMEM solution with transfection neurobasal medium through pipetting.
Incubate the mixture for 20–30 minutes at 37°C.
Transfer coverslips to a 12-well plate filled with 400 μL of pre-warmed transfection neurobasal medium using autoclaved fine forceps.
Return the 12-well plate and medium used for maintaining neuronal cells to the incubator.
Treat each coverslip with 100 μL of transfection solution drop by drop using a 200 μL tip after the 20–30 minute incubation period.
Place the treated coverslips in an incubator for 4 hours.
Return the coverslips to their original 12-well plate using autoclaved fine forceps and place them back in the incubator.
Incubate dishes in a humidified incubator at 37°C with 5% CO₂ for approximately 48 hours to allow fluorescent protein expression.
Combine the coverslip with a quick-release imaging chamber (QR-48LP) two days after transfection.
Securely mount the chamber onto the environmental chamber stage.
Search the entire area by 20× magnification.
Save the positions of transfected pyramidal neurons through X/Y coordinate demarcation.
Switch to the 60× 1.40 NA objective lens and adjust focus.
Navigate designated neurons by the ND Acquisition tab and XY sub-tab.
Adjust the pinhole to 1.2 airy units.
Select a pixel size as X = 0.17 μm, Y = 0.17 μm for the 60× 1.40 NA lens.
Set a scan area of 256 pixels × 256 pixels.
Take 7 images over a 1.5 μm section at intervals of 0.25 μm.
Choose 4 images corresponding to the 1.0 μm section based on fluorescence intensity for measurement.
Adjust laser power to 8 μW, PMT gain (110 for 488 nm laser and 120 for 561 nm laser), and offset (0) for each channel to achieve optimal signal-to-noise ratio.
Use scan mode to adjust the field of view, centering on the secondary branches of apical neuronal dendrites.
Take images of mCherry and SEP-DAGLα in dendrites with two channels (488 nm and 561 nm) simultaneously before bleaching.
Two minutes after taking the image, use a 488 nm wavelength laser to bleach the SEP signal in the dendritic shaft centered on a single z-section with the strongest SEP-DAGLα intensity.
Set the region of interest to 12 μm (width) × 8 μm (height).
Stimulate the center of the dendrite for 5 seconds with an 820 μW laser power at 488 nm wavelength to bleach the SEP signal.
Immediately after photobleaching, record 7 images-Z-stacks with 2 channels (488 and 561 nm) at 0.25 μm intervals every 30 s for 21 times over 10 min.
